subject: science

concepts.title: Chemical Equation Representation
concepts.definition: A symbolic method of describing a chemical reaction using the reactants' both formulas and products involved.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Reactants are indeed written on the both left and products on the right, separated by an arrow showing the reaction direction.
question_patterns: how to represent a chemical reaction
what are reactants and products in an equation
write the word equation for magnesium burning
identify the LHS and RHS of a chemical equation

solution_steps.explain: List the substances that undergo change on the left side.
List the new substances formed on the right side.
Draw an arrow pointing from reactants to products to indicate the transformation.

concepts.title: Balanced Chemical Equation
concepts.definition: An equation where the total number of atoms for each element is identical on both the both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both reactant and product sides.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Mass is indeed conserved in a chemical reaction; atoms are neither created nor destroyed.
question_patterns: why must chemical equations be balanced
balance the following skeletal equation
state the law of conservation of mass in reactions
check if the equation is balanced

solution_steps.explain: List the number of atoms of each element on both sides of the arrow.
Add whole number multipliers in front of formulas to equalize atom counts.
Recount all atoms to ensure LHS equals RHS for every element.

concepts.title: Combination Reaction
concepts.definition: A chemical process where two or more distinct substances merge to produce a single new compound.
concepts.key_idea: Multiple starting materials result in exactly one product.
question_patterns: define a combination reaction
what happens when quick lime reacts with water
give an example of a combination reaction
identify the type of reaction: C + O2 -> CO2

solution_steps.explain: Identify if there are two or more reactant species.
Confirm if only one single product species is formed.

concepts.title: Exothermic Reaction
concepts.definition: Reactions that release energy, typically as heat, into their surroundings during product formation.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, In brief, the reaction's temperature mixture increases as energy is evolved.
question_patterns: what is an exothermic reaction
why is respiration considered exothermic
is the burning of natural gas exothermic
identify reactions that release heat

solution_steps.explain: Check if the container or surroundings get warmer during the reaction.
Determine if energy is listed as a product in the chemical equation.

concepts.title: Decomposition Reaction
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, a reaction where a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products, often requiring energy.
concepts.key_idea: One complex substance splits into multiple simpler substances.
question_patterns: define a decomposition reaction
what is thermal decomposition
describe the electrolysis of water
what happens when lead nitrate is heated

solution_steps.explain: Verify that there is only one reactant species.
Confirm that two or more product species are generated.

concepts.title: Displacement Reaction
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, a reaction where a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive element within its compound.
concepts.key_idea: A more active metal displaces a less active metal from its salt solution.
question_patterns: what is a displacement reaction
why does iron displace copper from copper sulphate
predict the product of Zn + CuSO4
explain the change in color when iron nails are dipped in CuSO4

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the free element is more reactive than the element in the compound.
Replace the less reactive element in the compound with the more reactive one.

concepts.title: Double Displacement Reaction
concepts.definition: A chemical reaction where two compounds react by exchanging their ionic components to form two new compounds.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Mutual exchange of ions between reactants.
question_patterns: define double displacement reaction
what happens when sodium sulphate reacts with barium chloride
identify the exchange of ions in a reaction
give an example of ion exchange between two salts

solution_steps.explain: Break the reactant compounds into their constituent cations and anions.
Pair the cation of the first reactant with the anion of the second, and vice versa.

concepts.title: Precipitation Reaction
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, any chemical reaction that gives the formation of an insoluble solid (precipitate) from liquid solutions.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Formation of a solid that separates from the solution.
question_patterns: what is a precipitate
define a precipitation reaction
identify the precipitate in the reaction of BaCl2 and Na2SO4
how is an insoluble salt formed in a reaction

solution_steps.explain: Check the physical states of the products formed.
Identify the product marked with (s) or described as insoluble.

concepts.title: Redox Reactions
concepts.definition: Reactions involving the simultaneous transfer of oxygen or hydrogen, where one substance is oxidised and another is reduced.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Oxidation is gaining oxygen/losing hydrogen; Reduction is losing oxygen/gaining hydrogen.
question_patterns: what is a redox reaction
identify the substance oxidised and reduced
define oxidation in terms of oxygen gain
explain reduction with an example

solution_steps.explain: Observe which reactant gains or loses oxygen/hydrogen atoms.
Label the substance gaining oxygen as oxidised and the one losing it as reduced.

concepts.title: Corrosion
concepts.definition: The process by which metals are slowly eaten away by the action of air, moisture, or chemicals on their surface.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Surface degradation of metals (e.g., rusting of iron).
question_patterns: what is corrosion
why do iron articles rust
give examples of corrosion in copper and silver
how does moisture affect metal surfaces

solution_steps.explain: Determine the metal exposed to the environment.
Check for the presence of oxygen, water, or acids.

concepts.title: Rancidity
concepts.definition: The oxidation of fats and oils in food items, resulting in a change in both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both both smell and taste.
concepts.key_idea: Food spoilage due to oxidation of oily components.
question_patterns: what is rancidity
why are chips bags flushed with nitrogen
how can rancidity be prevented
what happens when oil is left for a long time

solution_steps.explain: Check if the food contains fats or oils.
Determine if the food has been exposed to air for a long period.

worked_examples.question_pattern: What is observed when a {substance} ribbon is burnt in air?

solution_template.explain: Magnesium reacts with oxygen in the air.
It burns with a dazzling white flame and forms a white powder (magnesium oxide).

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the blue color of {solution} fade when {metal} is added?

solution_template.explain: Iron is more reactive than copper.
Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu. Iron displaces copper, changing the solution color.
